message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 260, "amount_cents": 8294}, {"order_id": 263, "amount_cents": 8982}, {"order_id": 265, "amount_cents": 10903}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: I need to compare the refunds reported by Alpha Co with our records to ensure they match before proceeding with payouts. I will retrieve the list of refunds from our system.
The refunds reported by Alpha Co match exactly with our records. There are no discrepancies, so I can proceed to calculate each customer's net balance using the net_balance tool.

The net_balance tool returned an error indicating that customer '260' does not exist. This suggests that the customer identifier might not be the order ID. I need to investigate further to find the correct customer identifier associated with the refunds. First, I will list all orders to see if there is a connection between order IDs and customer IDs.
I found that order_id 260 belongs to customer 'acme'. The net_balance tool requires a customer identifier, not an order_id. I will now retrieve the net balance for customer 'acme'.
I have the net balance for customer 'acme' as 29089 cents. Next, I need to get the net balance for customer 'birch'.
I have the net balance for customer 'birch' as 62075 cents. Next, I need to get the net balance for customer 'cobalt'.
I have the net balances for all customers: acme (29089), birch (62075), and cobalt (39438). Now I will record the payouts for each customer.
I have successfully recorded the payout for customer 'acme'. Now I will record the payout for customer 'birch'.

result.error: bad arguments: World.record_payout() got an unexpected keyword argument 'amount_ cents'. Did you mean 'amount_cents'?

reply.thought: I made a typo in the argument name 'amount_ cents' instead of 'amount_cents'. I will correct this and record the payout for customer  'birch' again.
I see that there was a typo in the tool name 'record_ payout' with an extra space. I need to correct this and use the correct tool name 'record_payout' to record the payout for customer  'birch'.
I have successfully recorded the payout for customer 'birch'. Now I will record the payout for customer 'cobalt'.
I made a typo in the tool name again. I need to use the correct tool name 'record_payout' without any space.
All payouts have been successfully recorded for customers acme, birch, and cobalt. The batch is now complete.
